podcast.title: Tragic Death in Dublin (July 3, 1986)
podcast.body: On July 3, 1986, Greg Carroll was involved in a fatal motorcycle accident in Dublin while on a courier run for U2. A car cut in front of him on rain-slicked streets, and he was unable to stop in time, resulting in an instant fatality. "But then on July 3, 1986, Greg was sent off on a courier run on his motorcycle in Dublin, a car cut in front of him. And because of rain slick streets, he was unable to stop at time. Carroll T-bone the car and was killed instantly."

podcast.title: Dedications by U2
podcast.body: U2 dedicated both their iconic 1987 album "The Joshua Tree" and the song "One Tree Hill" to the memory of their beloved roadie, Greg Carroll, solidifying his legacy within the band's history. "Both One Tree Hill and the Joshua Tree are dedicated to the memory of Rody Greg Carroll."

podcast.title: Friendship with U2
podcast.body: During his time with U2, Greg Carroll became close friends with Bono, Bono's wife Ali, the rest of the band members, and the wider crew, indicating his well-liked personality and strong integration into the U2 organization. "Carroll became friends with Bono, his wife Allie, the rest of the band, and the rest of the crew. Everybody loved this guy."

podcast.title: Funeral Attended by U2
podcast.body: Following his death, Greg Carroll's body was flown back to New Zealand, and members of U2 traveled to attend his funeral ceremony, underscoring their deep respect and grief. "Carroll's body was flown back to New Zealand. Members of U2 went to the funeral."

podcast.title: Local Roadie for U2
podcast.body: Greg Carroll was a local roadie from Auckland, New Zealand, initially hired by U2 to assist with production during their "Unforgettable Fire" tour in Australia and New Zealand in 1984. His exceptional performance led U2 manager Paul McGuinness to hire him for the remainder of the tour. "He was a local Rody hired to help out with their production."

podcast.title: Profound Impact on U2
podcast.body: Greg Carroll's death had a profound and lasting effect on everyone within the U2 organization, highlighting his importance and the personal connections he had formed with the band and crew. "His death had a profound effect on everybody in the U2 organization."

xref.title: Guitar Parts for "One Tree Hill"
xref.body: The Edge contributed his distinctive guitar parts to the U2 song "One Tree Hill." These parts, combined with Bono's lyrics and the efforts of Toronto musicians, helped finalize the track dedicated to roadie Greg Carroll. "With Bono's lyrics, the edges guitar parts and contributions from three Toronto musicians at Grant Avenue Studios in Hamilton, the song was finished."
